theory.intro: Rounding replaces a number with the nearest 'round' number — a multiple of $10$, $100$, $1000$ and so on.
facts: Look at the digit **just to the right** of the rounding place.
If it is $5$ or more, round **up**; if it is $4$ or less, round **down**.
Every digit after the rounding place becomes $0$.
steps: Underline the digit in the place you are rounding to.
Check the next digit on its right.
Round up or stay, then fill the rest with zeros.

foundation.question_text: Round the census count $84\,352$ to the nearest hundred.
Round a distance of $267\,430$ m to the nearest thousand metres.
Round $3\,764\,210$ to the nearest ten thousand.
A region's population is $6\,581\,900$. Round it to the nearest hundred thousand.

development.question_text: A national census records $24\,650\,000$ people. Round this to the nearest million.
Round the surveyed distance $7\,999\,650$ m to the nearest thousand metres.
Round $82\,149\,999$ to the nearest ten thousand.
A map gives a route length of $1\,250\,000$ m. Round it to the nearest hundred thousand metres.
Which place was $73\,846\,219$ rounded to if the result is $73\,800\,000$?
development.solution_text:
The last five digits became zero, so the hundred-thousands digit was rounded.
The number was rounded to the nearest hundred thousand.

development.question_text: A population of $54\,499\,999$ is reported to the nearest million. What is the rounded population?

mastery.question_text: A whole-number census count rounds to $8\,300\,000$ to the nearest hundred thousand. What is the smallest possible count?
mastery.solution_text:
The halfway point below $8\,300\,000$ is $8\,250\,000$.
Smallest possible count $=8\,250\,000$

mastery.question_text: A whole-number distance rounds to $47\,000$ m to the nearest thousand metres. What is the largest possible distance?
mastery.solution_text:
$47\,500$ m would round up to $48\,000$ m.
Largest possible distance $=47\,499$ m

mastery.question_text: A report rounds the same count to $6\,420\,000$ to the nearest ten thousand and to $6\,400\,000$ to the nearest hundred thousand. Give one possible original count.
mastery.solution_text:
$6\,421\,000$ rounds to $6\,420\,000$ to the nearest ten thousand.
It also rounds to $6\,400\,000$ to the nearest hundred thousand.
One possible count is $6\,421\,000$.
